claim.text: On one genuinely upstream-authored public-domain Prolog program, the unmodified file is rejected by the Rust lexer's lack of block comments, whereas a one-comment-only normalized derivative reproduces twelve live SWI-Prolog ordered results in both frozen Rust engines.
claim.scope: SWI-Prolog/swipl-devel/demo/likes.pl pinned to 111385b9, 12 atom-only queries on native ELF64; original source unchanged; Gen18/Gen19 source SHAs immutable.
assumptions: The original file and demo README are byte-identical to pinned upstream Git blobs
Deleting the one source documentation block does not alter Prolog clauses or fact order
The SWI output translator only accepts a flat ordered list of lowercase atoms
Actual SWI 9.0.4 and Rust 1.85.1 perform only the bounded tests
forbidden_promotions: Do not label the unmodified original as Rust-supported
Do not infer full ISO/GNU Prolog conformance or native performance
Do not call the comment-only derived program independently unmodified
Do not treat project-authored query selection and translation as independent experimental authorship

specification.intended_object: Pinned original upstream source with explicit syntax support classification and live independent SWI-Prolog reference, compared to two immutable Rust subset CLIs after one disclosed comment removal.
invariants: Git blob SHA1 original likes.pl and upstream public-domain README exact
Exactly one /** <examples> ... */ comment removed; original bytes retained
Unmodified original rust parse error at byte 440, exit 2 on both versions
12 reference cases exact SWI-to-Rust ordered outputs, stderr and exit
Final-head fixed Rust max-solutions 32 and max-steps 100000 for all 12 queries
known_answer_cases: SWI likes(sam,Food) yields nine ordered foods
SWI likes(sam,curry) and unknown yield no solutions
Rust original parser unsupported block-comment byte

implementation.commit: upstream 111385b90852dade2b772d074cc55fefa20ee1a9; released Rust 901c8b58c12fbe8b79f70b0118f951f3ed2fcf21; retired Rust c09fff05d9b3dd43fb90014278e3a98d701d3640
implementation.environment: Ubuntu 24.04 ELF64; SWI-Prolog 9.0.4 system interpreter; Rust 1.85.1 release feature disabled; Python 3 standard library
implementation.live_entrypoint: Original source loaded into external swipl -f none -s likes.pl; findall/3+write_canonical/1; Rust gprolog-rs CLI accepts strictly comment-normalized temporary file
implementation.representation: Original 922-byte file, normalized 797-byte derivative; plain-atom ordered binding stdout, negative parser stderr and exit code

metric.name: Typed per-query SWI/Rust ordered answer parity, status and original-file parser compatibility
metric.units: 12 exact ordered answer vectors, status/stderr equality, one original parser incompatibility, 264 historical comparison flags
equivalence_attacks: Raw upstream file with documentation block versus comment-normalized derivative
Positive and negative ground likes/2 queries
Ordered enumerated foods versus individual ground cases
Two frozen Rust engines against live SWI output

black_box: Live external SWI-Prolog evaluation on exact original source for 12 frozen queries
Each Rust version's normalized derivative CLI output compared exactly with SWI converted plain atoms
264 strict full stdout/stderr/exit historical Rust CLI differential
structural: Git SHA-1 upstream source and README license verified before normalization
One and only one doc block removed and preserved as SHA256
Original Rust parse failure classified at byte 440 for both versions
SWI version and source SHA256 recorded
property_based: not applicable: fixed one-source externally authored compatibility case, not randomized population
metamorphic: Comment removed without changing clause tokens
positive vs negative ground query and full enumeration
two Rust implementations same ordered results
fuzzing: not applicable: inherited 264-case regression corpus only, not new independent fuzzing
historical: Gen18 and retired Gen19 source trees are pinned immutable
Gen23 prior 12 external relation but author-reconstructed workload claims are kept separate

matched_baselines: Original upstream file executed by independent SWI engine
Comment-normalized derivative executed by released Gen18 and rejected Gen19 CLIs
negative_controls: Unmodified original fails parser due slash at byte 440
Ground true cases across three recipe branches and chips fact
controls.compute_parity: Both Rust versions built with same Rust 1.85.1 release flags and ELF64. SWI is not timed nor a performance peer.
controls.parameter_parity: Same fixed queries, 32 max solutions, 100000 max steps for each Rust variant.
controls.sampling_parity: One execution per query and version in CI, plus 264 historical differential; not an inferential runtime sample.
controls.data_access_parity: SWI consumes untouched Git-pinned original; Rust consumes only temporary comment-stripped derivative with SHA256 identity; semantic clause sequence preserved by assumption and byte-level transform.

preregistration.prediction: Original source must fail Rust parsing at one unsupported block comment; one comment-only removal yields programs with 12 SWI matching ordered answers across both frozen Rust versions.
preregistration.primary_metric: Full 12-query ordered result/status vector plus original parser rejection and exact source preservation; no execution-time metric.
preregistration.uncertainty_method: Deterministic replay once per query/version; limited single source program, interpreter and machine; no confidence intervals or general workloads.
preregistration.kill_condition: Missing source hash/licensing, unexpected normalized edits, original accepted unexpectedly, SWI missing or error, unsupported SWI term type, any Rust/SWI mismatch or 264-case regression.
preregistration.stop_condition: No clause rewrites, parser feature additions or ownership optimization to rescue unsupported syntax or semantic mismatch in this experiment.
preregistration.promotion_rule: M only for the bounded external-source comment-compatibility and 12 ordered semantic comparisons after exact-head independent SWI evidence and controls pass.

execution_records: The initial run used a reference-derived solution cap; the final-head fixed-32 cap correction must pass before merge

result.observed: Initial run 44367811617: pinned upstream source rejected by both Rust lexers at byte 440 (0x2f), and comment-normalized derivative matched 12/12 live SWI-Prolog 9.0.4 ordered outputs on both frozen Rust CLIs; 264 historical Rust full-output comparisons passed. Final fixed-cap reproduction must be verified.
result.effect_size: 12/12 correct ordered SWI/Gen18 and SWI/Gen19 comparisons, 1 explicitly identified source lexer incompatibility, 264/264 historical regressions.
result.uncertainty: Only a single public-domain teaching file and 12 project-selected queries, SWI is an independent engine but the experiment itself is project-authored; original is not directly supported and only a comment-normalized derivative is executed on Rust.
retired_claims: Description of project-reconstructed Gen23 fixtures as independently authored programs
Equating a successful derived-source comparison to unmodified upstream compatibility
active_remainder: Additional unmodified upstream workloads with wider syntax
Independent full ISO Prolog conformance and representative benchmarks
